title: SlimSLAM: An Adaptive Runtime for Visual-Inertial Simultaneous Localization and Mapping
problem: SLAM algorithms must achieve both speed and accuracy for real-time performance in AR/VR and robotics, but accurate SLAM is computationally expensive while platforms are resource-constrained. Designers face a trade-off: pay for specialized accelerators or sacrifice algorithm accuracy.
motivation: Accurate SLAM is essential to prevent motion sickness in AR/VR headsets and navigation errors in autonomous robots and drones, yet computational constraints prevent real-time execution on typical platforms.
method: SLAM (simultaneous localization and mapping—tracking your position while building a map from camera and motion sensors) must be fast enough for real-time AR/VR and robotics, but accurate algorithms are computationally expensive on resource-constrained devices. SlimSLAM solves this by having a runtime that monitors available computing resources and automatically adjusts the algorithm's complexity—using full-featured processing when resources allow and simpler approximations when resources are tight. This maintains accurate pose estimation (precise positioning) in real-time, regardless of the device's computational power.
key_novelty: SlimSLAM maintains accurate SLAM performance in real-time across resource-constrained devices by dynamically adjusting algorithm complexity based on available computational resources.
contributions: Adaptive runtime framework for visual-inertial SLAM
Dynamic algorithm tuning mechanism to balance accuracy and latency
Real-time SLAM support on constrained platforms without specialized hardware
